limitations: Benchmark performance is not a complete measure of general intelligence.

An attribution error and a false capability assessment are different questions.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI did not exceed the intelligence of all people by the end of 2025, contrary to Musk's prediction.

statement.document_title: Elon Musk’s preposterous and possibly harmful claim about robotic surgery

from_speaker: AI would exceed the intelligence of all people

our_interpretation: Assess the normalized proposition about AI capability by December 31, 2025. The wager amounts are contextual, not company financial claims.
The ordinary reading is general intellectual superiority to the strongest humans, not merely better scores on one test.
'All people' could instead mean humanity collectively. That stronger reading must not be silently substituted for superiority to any individual.
Treat the attribution to Musk separately from whether the capability milestone occurred.
The target period is calendar 2025, with the decisive status assessed at its end.
criteria.support_condition: Broad, credible evidence covering the end of 2025 establishes that available AI systems had not reached general intellectual superiority to the strongest humans under an ordinary reading of that threshold.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Validated evidence shows that an AI system had achieved that broad general superiority by December 31, 2025.

evidence.explanation: Contemporary reporting assigns the collective-human threshold to 2029 and separately reports a prediction about any one human around the end of 2025. This raises an attribution ambiguity; it does not determine AI capability in 2025.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A broad, independently validated assessment of late-2025 systems against strong human baselines, together with the original prediction's wording and a clear individual-versus-collective interpretation.
